thread.title: (Gallery) Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years. Here's who led the charge in the Triad

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: (Gallery) Q2's profit surge was the strongest in years. Here's who led the charge in the Triad
text: – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Sep 4, 2018, 7:15am EDT U.S. companies rebounded from a lackluster showing in the first quarter of the year with a surge in profits that's expected to fuel even more economic growth in the months ahead. The Commerce Department reported this week that after-tax profits among U.S. companies jumped 16.1 percent on a year-over-year during the quarter that ended June 30, qualifying as the largest such increase since 2012. The boom was especially pronounced in the banking industry, which pocketed more after-tax profits than any other sector in Q2. Among U.S. financial companies, profits increased $16.8 billion in the second quarter, in contrast to a decrease of $9.3 billion in the first quarter. Meanwhile, the Commerce Department reported that profits at non-financial corporations increased $63.6 billion, compared with an increase of $32.3 billion. A Business Journals analysis of more than 3,000 publicly traded companies found that the electronics components sector saw the largest profit gains over the same period in 2017. The sector reported $15.9 billion in profit during the second quarter — $8.5 billion more than what it earned during the year-earlier period. Warren Buffett 's Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK.A) posted the largest quarterly profit of any public company in the second quarter, and it also posted the strongest year-over-year gain. The Omaha, Nebraska-based investment company netted $12 billion last quarter, marking a $7.8 billion increase over 2017's corresponding period. Berkshire’s success narrowly beat the world’s first trillion-dollar company. Apple’s (Nasdaq: AAPL) second-quarter profits topped $11.5 billion, a $2.8 billion improvement from a year earlier. Rounding out the top five were Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT), which earned $8.9 billion (up $804 million); JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM), with $8.3 billion (up $1.3 billion); and Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), with $6.9 billion (up $1.7 billion). For the most part, Triad companies also saw significant second-quarter profits, with BB&T Corp. (NYSE: BBT) leading the way with $819 million, a $144 million increase from the year before. Also in the top five are: Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings (NYSE: LH), with $233.8 million in profits (up $49 million) Old Dominion Freight Line Inc. (Nasdaq: ODFL), with $163.4 million (up $65 million) VF Corp. (NYSE: VFC), with $160 million (up $50 million) Hanesbrands Inc. (NYSE: HBI), with $140 million (down $31.9 million) – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Sep 4, 2018, 7:15am EDT Related Content
